the importance of the distance from the mini-implants to the alveolar crest in order to avoid the risk of mini-implants failure.
the relationship between the distance from the implant to the bone crest, the age of the patient and the success of orthopedic miniscrews.
the importance of the DC distance in the long-term success of MI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the distance to the AC should be at least 5 mm to achieve long-term stability of orthodontic MIs.
the distance to the alveolar crest should be at least 5 mm for orthodontic miniscrew implants.
the distance to the alveolar crest and the root proximity should be considered when selecting an implant location.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distance to alveolo crestal bone is a critical factor in orthodontic mini-screw success rate.
the distance between the mini-implants and the alveolar crest is a key factor for the stability of orthodontic MIs, and this factor should be considered in the design of orthodontic treatment plans.
the closer the mini-implants are to the crestal bone, the higher is the probability of their failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distance between the MI and the alveolar crest should be greater than 5 mm.
the success of MI placement should be based on the distance of the implant to the AC, and not to the root proximity.
the distance to the AC should be taken into account in the treatment planning of orthodontic MIs.
